gaps.sentence: Nobody explained the reason ___ the flight was cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Why' introduces the cause after 'the reason'; it means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: We must decide ___ to do next.
gaps.explanation: 'What to do' is the standard pattern meaning 'the thing that we should do'.

gaps.sentence: He is a colleague on ___ you can always depend.
gaps.explanation: After 'on', the formal relative pronoun for a person is 'whom'.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: My uncle, ___ lives in Canada, is coming to stay next week.
gaps.hint: non-defining clause after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses (between commas) 'that' is not allowed; 'who' refers to people.

gaps.sentence: The Eiffel Tower, ___ attracts millions of visitors, was completed in 1889.
gaps.explanation: For things in non-defining clauses use 'which'; 'that' is not allowed after a comma.
'What happened next' means 'the thing that happened'; 'that' cannot introduce the clause here because the sentence needs a subject inside it.
